hypothesis: A power cut at any sector write of the write service's scenario leaves a volume that recovers to fsck.fat-clean state with every synced byte intact.
narrative:
checks/fat32-rw.py builds a mkfs.fat FAT32 volume with 512-byte clusters at sector 32768 of a card image, and runs a scenario through the service while the model logs every sector write. The scenario creates a directory and a long-named, preallocated file with two syncs and a close, replaces a configuration file, renames a file over another, unlinks and truncates. For every cut point, a power cut leaves the first k logged sectors. The check then runs mount-time recovery, runs fsck.fat -n (exit status 0 required), reads the volume with an independent Python FAT32 reader and compares each file with the constraints the scenario recorded, and mounts again to confirm that nothing is written. The independent reader stands in for mtools, which is not installed on the host. Results of the committed run: 1339 cuts (one per sector write of the scenario), 2482 random subsets of multi-sector calls, 133 cuts in the recovery itself, all clean with synced bytes intact.
The sweep found one defect during development: the recovery's last write cleared the clean bit in FAT copy 1 before copy 2, so a cut between them left FAT 1 clean and FAT 2 different, and the volume mounted without recovery. The flag now clears in copy 2 first and sets in copy 1 first; the sweep fails on the earlier ordering. Skipping the freeing of unclaimed clusters (a mutation of the recovery) makes the sweep fail with fsck.fat reporting lost clusters.
Other checks in the same file: write-size accounting (20000 appends of 100 bytes become 30 writes of one AU each, none unaligned, each preceded by a yield), the write guard at every region boundary, and the POSIX-like calls through the newlib system calls with a descriptor limit, would-block writes that touch nothing, truncate-replace visibility, rename over an existing file, ftruncate and posix_fallocate. checks/sunxi-mmc-write-dma.c runs a 128 KiB write with 4 ms of DMA and 300 ms of busy: 172 polls and 154 sleeps, one of them on the interrupt; it also covers an interrupt that arrives before the sleep, one that is lost, and stale and spurious wakes.
Linux comparison (reference fs/fat, stable tree linux-6.12.y): the service differs deliberately in three ways. Dirty flag: fat_set_state sets and clears FAT_STATE_DIRTY in the boot sector's state byte at mount and in fat_put_super and warns "Volume was not properly unmounted"; this service records the state in FAT[1] bit 27 because the boot sector is outside the writable regions and fsck.fat reads FAT[1], and sets it lazily before the first metadata write. Ordering at fsync: fat_file_fsync calls __generic_file_fsync (data pages, then the inode holding the directory entry), then sync_mapping_buffers on the FAT inode, then blkdev_issue_flush, so the directory entry reaches the device before the FAT blocks; this service writes the FAT chain before the directory entry so that an entry never names a chain the FAT does not hold. FSInfo: fat_clusters_flush copies the free count and next-free hint into the FSInfo buffer and writes it back with the superblock; this service does the same at checkpoint and unmount. Agreement: the FAT copies are written in order (fat_mirror_bhs); a new directory cluster is zeroed before it is linked; a deleted file marks its short and long-name entries deleted (fat_remove_entries), where Linux can leave orphaned long-name entries after a cut and entry_delete here deletes long entries in other sectors first, so a cut leaves a valid file under its short name.

hypothesis: The host plan for creating the 512 MiB region file on the 62.5 GB card names every sector range the write may touch and the 395-sector backup.
prediction:
The card holds one FAT32 partition at sector 32,768 (MBR type 0x0C) with 122,105,856 sectors, 64 sectors per cluster, 64 reserved sectors, two FATs of 14,912 sectors, FSInfo at partition sector 1, backup boot sector at 6 and root cluster 2; the volume is labelled "64 GB DRIVE" and was clean and empty beyond its root cluster when read. The read-only backup probe (apps/sd-backup-probe) read the SD Status register on the board: AU_SIZE is 9, so the allocation unit is 4 MiB, 8,192 sectors, and UHS_AU_SIZE reads the same. It returned 457 listed sectors (the MBR, the boot area, both FATs through index 159, and the root cluster) with the restoration words unchanged; the dump is under ~/.cache/sunstoneos/sd-backup/.
The host run fat32-rw plan creates /sunstone-test/sunstone-region-test.bin (536,870,912 bytes) on a mkfs.fat volume of this geometry with this allocation unit and records every write:
| Set | Absolute sectors | Count | Backed up |
| MBR | 0 | 1 (read only; it gives the partition) | yes |
| Boot area: boot sector, FSInfo, backup boot sector, backup FSInfo | 32,768 to 32,775 | 8 (only FSInfo, 32,769, is written) | yes |
| FAT copy 1, indexes 0 to 128 | 32,832 to 32,960 | 129 | yes |
| FAT copy 2, indexes 0 to 128 | 47,744 to 47,872 | 129 | yes |
| Root cluster 2 and directory cluster 3 (sunstone-test) | 62,656 to 62,783 | 128 | yes |
| Data, clusters 47 to 16,430 (first cluster on an allocation unit boundary) | 65,536 to 1,114,111 | 1,048,576 | no: the approval record lists it as data |
The write ranges are FSInfo [32769, 1], both FATs, [62656, 128] and the data. The backup is 395 sectors in five ranges ([0,1] [32768,8] [32832,129] [47744,129] [62656,128]). The service writes 267 metadata sectors and the data in 4,110 calls: 4,096 data pieces of 256 sectors and 14 metadata writes. The boot sector, its backup, the backup FSInfo and every other FAT sector are never written. The data start follows the allocation unit, so the plan is regenerated for a different card.
conclusion: The plan was carried out: the file exists in a contiguous chain from cluster 47 to 16430 (entries 1793623788842205312-60954030, 1793632378497932347-1618d4a8; read back by 1793632483097936083-744016a7 and 1793632486531867079-fd56b38d). A later session's backup differs from the first capture because a session changes the very sectors the backup holds; the per-session procedure is in the design. The v14 mode 2 run showed it: all 395 sectors were read and the hash differed.
narrative: The 457-sector read-only probe is entry 1793612289390889939-c86b87e7. The first capture (backup-395-sectors.bin, the card before any write) is the restore point and is never replaced.
